children: The chips are built on an advanced 2nm process node and are powered by Qualcomm's custom Oryon CPU; the Extreme Gen 6 chip version supports 8K recording at 60fps and 4K at 240fps

Qualcomm has introduced two new flagship smartphone processors, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, as the chipmaker doubles down on agentic AI experiences that run directly on the device rather than in the cloud.

Unveiled at the Snapdragon Summit in Maui, Hawaii, the two platforms mark Qualcomm's first dual-flagship strategy, giving device makers a choice between its most powerful silicon yet and a slightly scaled-down variant that still carries most of the same headline features.
Built for the Agentic AI Age

Both chips are designed to support AI agents capable of understanding user behaviour, distinguishing between speakers, and building local memory from device usage patterns. Qualcomm said the platforms can run small AI models of up to 200 million parameters through a new sensing hub, handling tasks such as speaker identification and local transcription without routing data to the cloud.

The Extreme variant goes further, capable of running a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model entirely on-device, alongside a complete voice-in, voice-out AI agent that builds memory from user interactions to offer more personalised suggestions and task automation.

"Today marks a milestone as we introduce not one, but two new flagship mobile platforms, delivering agentic AI experiences that are immediate, personal, and adaptive," said Chris Patrick, Senior Vice President and General Manager of Mobile Handsets at Qualcomm Technologies. He added that the dual-platform approach allows the company to push technical boundaries while giving OEMs greater choice in shaping the next generation of intelligent, personalised mobile experiences.

Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon framed the shift in broader terms during his keynote, noting that AI will require devices to do far more than execute commands, moving away from app navigation and towards completing tasks on the user's behalf.

The move puts Qualcomm alongside other chipmakers racing to bring larger AI models onto consumer hardware. Apple, for comparison, introduced a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model as part of its third-generation foundation models at WWDC in June.
Beyond AI, both platforms are built on an advanced 2nm process node and are powered by Qualcomm's custom Oryon CPU, a rearchitected Adreno GPU, and the Hexagon NPU.

On the camera front, the chips bring pixel-level control, improved stabilisation and motion understanding, with the Extreme version supporting 8K recording at 60fps and 4K at 240fps, alongside Qualcomm's Advanced Professional Video (APV) codec. Both platforms use AI to enhance call quality, with a feature called Voice Bubble designed to isolate the user's voice and reduce background noise.
Gaming also gets a boost through Adreno Neural Fusion, which uses AI to deliver more intelligent graphics rendering, richer visuals and longer playtime.
Motorola has already confirmed a device built on the new platform. The Motorola Signature 27 will run on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, with general availability expected later this year.

Beyond Motorola, Qualcomm named a broader roster of OEM partners set to bring devices powered by the two platforms to market, including Honor, iQOO, Nubia, OnePlus, OPPO, REDMI, RedMagic, vivo, Xiaomi and ZTE.

The announcement is part of Qualcomm's wider push to position the smartphone as a central platform for AI, with the company noting it is working on more than 40 AI-focused devices as the industry continues weighing how much AI processing can realistically shift from the cloud onto the handset itself.
